title: AI guardrails wrapper and offline evaluation harness
acceptance: src/ai/guardrails.mjs exports a wrapper that every provider call goes through; neutralises injection markers ('ignore previous instructions', role tags like <system>/[INST]/'system:') in document text, with tests
Input larger than the configured cap is truncated or rejected deterministically; tested
For cloud providers names, phones, emails, SSN/MBI patterns and plates are redacted before the call; the local provider receives full text; tested for both
Outputs are validated against src/ai/schemas.mjs task schemas; invalid output is rejected and falls back (no throw); tested
tests/fixtures/ai/golden/*.json holds golden cases for each task on synthetic scenarios (fictional data only)

node src/ai/eval.mjs scores the local provider: extraction field precision/recall, severity band accuracy, fraud/subrogation flag accuracy, and writes docs/ai-evaluation.md with method and table; vertex providers scored only on recorded fake responses
brief: Read src/ai/index.mjs, cascade.mjs, schemas.mjs, inference-log.mjs and providers/* first. Build guardrails.mjs as a pure, zero-dependency layer: sanitizeText(text, opts) for injection neutralisation (replace markers with a visible [removed-instruction] token, never execute; also strip role tags and fenced 'system' blocks, case-insensitive), capInput(text, maxChars) with a default and a flag reporting truncation, redact(text) with regexes for emails, US phones, SSN (###-##-####), MBI (11 char pattern), licence plates, and names (use a small fictional-name heuristic plus field-aware redaction of known structured fields such as claimant.name; keep placeholder tokens like [NAME_1] consistent within one call, and provide a reverse map used only locally). guard(provider, task) returns a wrapped provider with the same interface as existing providers: sanitize+cap, redact only when provider.kind/locality is cloud (check how _shared.mjs and local.mjs identify themselves; do not edit providers or cascade, since you cannot write src/ai/providers), call, then validate output against the task schema; on invalid return the cascade's existing fallback signal (inspect cascade.mjs for how failure is represented) and record via inference-log. Do not modify existing files outside your paths; if wiring into cascade is needed, document it as a contract-change request to the architecture hub and export a helper instead. eval.mjs: load golden JSON, run local provider per task, compute precision/recall per field, severity band accuracy, flag accuracy, plus replay recorded fake vertex responses stored in golden fixtures; export a runEval() function (tests call it with a tiny golden set) and a CLI mode that writes docs/ai-evaluation.md (method section, per-task table, date). Pitfalls: keep output deterministic (no timestamps that break diffs other than a date line), no real names or carriers, no network.

verdicts.reason: All criteria met; 18 tests pass, eval runs offline and regenerates docs, redaction/validation/fallback verified, logs hash-only, synthetic data
